Bathing a cat is generally not necessary because cats are fastidious self-groomers that keep themselves clean and maintain healthy skin and coat through natural oils [d2,d3,d4,d7,d10,d11]. Most healthy indoor cats rarely, if ever, require a bath unless they become dirty or encounter substances they should not ingest [d2,d3,d4,d7,d10,d11].

However, there are specific situations where bathing may be necessary or beneficial, such as when a cat gets into something toxic and risks ingesting it while grooming [d5,d8,d9,d11], when a cat has mobility or health issues that prevent adequate self-grooming [d5,d10,d11], or when a long-haired breed needs help preventing mats and tangles [d2,d3,d9]. In these cases, a bath can be a practical or even recommended intervention [d2,d3,d5,d9,d10,d11].
